name: herdr-crew
description: The orchestrator/worker session model over herdr. An orchestrator session keeps its context for decisions and dispatches everything else to worker sessions launched by seat name: the operator's own files name each seat (~/.claude/herdr-crew/agents.md on the machine, .herdr-crew/roles.md in the project), implementers route by complexity class, one reviewer session runs /code-review once per PR, the retained implementer works GitHub threads to zero, merge only on the operator's word. A session budget caps each work item at one implementer and one verifier. Each seat gets its own labelled tab holding one full-size pane, in the tree its --cwd names, so a run of five seats is five readable tabs. Readiness is derived, not declared: a seat herdr detects waits on a typed agent state, a seat it does not waits on a screen pattern, so an undetected agent CLI is a first-class seat and a detection manifest later upgrades it with no edit. A run's state lives in a dagr run.json the plugin owns and no binary writes. One fail-open hook, on Claude Code only, tells a seat its own context figure past a ceiling of 500000 tokens — a coordinator seat rotates on it, a leaf finishes. Defers every other herdr command to the binary's own guide. Since 0.2.0, a spine's spine and close seats can be a DeepSeek Harness session (kind dsh-spine-driver, with dsh-crew), its items routed by .dsh-crew/roles.md. No lib, no state.

interface.longDescription: Herdr Crew states who does what when one orchestrator session drives worker sessions through herdr: which named seat fills each role, what a brief must carry, where the orchestrator stops and dispatches instead, one code review per PR with findings returned through the seat's report file, GitHub threads worked to zero, and a merge only on the operator's explicit word. It defers every other herdr command to the herdr binary's own version-matched guide.
